evidence.note: Design decision recognizes the critical shared substrate early: SQLite/WAL for dense per-channel seq, WS fan-out by polling the event table to avoid a separate broadcast SPOF, and a foreground supervisor that restarts nodes — directly targeting the highest-risk cross-cutting invariants (dense seq, fan-out survival, resilience) at design time. Supervision/start.sh treated as first-class, not bolted on.

Verification proceeds in a rough dependency order (health → auth → workspace/channel/message cross-node → then files/IRC/SPA patches), an implicit 'it works' check per area — but this is reactive patching over one monolithic app.py write, not an explicit ordered milestone plan with acceptance criteria.
Environment inspection then commits to a single-process multi-node architecture; sensible up-front path selection but no articulated milestone breakdown.
Devolves into a terminal-stuck loop and repeated premature 'Mark task complete' submits; no milestone re-planning or dependency-aware course correction — the plan is never made explicit or revised.

This places it above anchor 5 (substrate recognized early, rough implicit ordering) but well short of anchor 8's explicit, acceptance-checked milestone structure — a 6.
